name: South Face

waypoints.name: Andrews Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Same long Pasayten Wilderness approach as other Cathedral Peak routes.
waypoints.directions: The drive is the simple part: from Winthrop, follow the Chewuch River valley north on West Chewuch Road / FR-51, paved the entire way, about 28 miles to the Andrews Creek Trailhead at roughly 3,040 ft. Andrews Creek Trail #504 leaves from the parking area; fill out the free self-issue wilderness permit here and leave a trailhead parking pass on the car. Most parties drive in and start walking toward the Upper Cathedral Lake basin the same day, so plan the drive around getting boots moving with daylight left. It is a two to four day trip from this lot, roughly 18 miles each way, so pack the car accordingly.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Peak summit
waypoints.note: Route climbs the ~1000' South Face wall, topping out at/near the true summit.

waypoints.name: Cathedral Peak South Face / Monk area pin

approach: The drive itself is easy — paved the whole way from Winthrop up the Chewuch River valley to the Andrews Creek Trailhead, about 28 miles total — but the climb to Cathedral Peak is one of the longest wilderness approaches in the state. From the trailhead, the Andrews Creek Trail (#504) climbs roughly 12 miles to 6,680+ ft Andrews Pass, then descends into the Spanish Creek drainage before a side trail climbs to Upper Cathedral Lakes below the peak's southwest side, putting the one-way approach at around 18 miles with significant elevation gain and loss along the way. Most parties treat this as a 2-4 day backpack (roughly 40+ miles round trip), camping at or near Cathedral Lakes before making a summit push. A free self-issue wilderness permit is required at the trailhead, along with a trailhead parking pass; the first many miles are a hot, rocky, buggy uphill slog with little shade, so this is genuinely a remote, multi-day alpine objective rather than a day-approach crag. For this specific route: from Cathedral Lakes camp, follow the trail toward Cathedral Pass and climb scree/talus to the base of the peak's main South Face and start low in the centre of the open wall, left of the deep gully that separates Cathedral Peak from The Monk (the SE Buttress starts inside that gully).
